# Trump says he’s keeping ‘status quo’ with Iran, with no need for new strikes

In an impromptu news conference, the president insisted negotiations are making progress.

4 min

President Donald Trump said there was little need for now to engage in an extensive new attack on Iran during a news conference on Monday. (Tierney L. Cross/Pool/For The Washington Post)

By Michael Birnbaum [...] The United States is unlikely to restart major military operations against Iran, President Donald Trump indicated Monday, saying he was satisfied that current negotiations were making progress and that there was little need for now to engage in an extensive new attack.

items.title: Donald Trump talks Iran, Pete Hegseth and Dana White at impromptu briefing
items.summary:
Trump downplayed renewing major military operations against Iran but signaled no end to the more than eight-month war. The president said he was maintaining a naval blockade against Iran, escalating a land blockade — dubbing it Operation Iron Gate — and offering protection to U.S. allies in the region.

Trump said the war was “ending quickly,” but added, “we want to take care of people that have been very good to us over the years.” [...] Trump said he talked to Huang on Monday, following the Nvidia CEO announcing he’d had an affair with a woman that the intelligence community reportedly alleges was a Chinese spy.

Trump called Huang “an honorable man” who “built a great American company.”

“I feel very confident he’ll be in good shape,” the president added.

Trump said he had no plans to bring up alleged Chinese corporate espionage in an expected summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping next week. [...] Trump said he heard about Huang’s association with the alleged spy “not too long ago.”

“When I heard about — first of all, I was amazed, because I view him as a very high-quality person,” the president said.

Trump added that he wasn’t aware of the allegations when he traveled to China to meet Xi in May. Trump hosted Xi for a state visit in September.

items.title: WATCH: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese agent | PBS News
items.summary:
# WATCH: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese agent

WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about the FBI looking into his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent.

President Donald Trump responded to spy plot allegations involving Nvidia's CEO in a White House briefing Monday. Watch his remarks in the player above. [...] "I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right, how you're doing," Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy."

President Donald Trump spoke about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy in a briefing Monday.

Trump is slated to meet next week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, but he was noncommittal about bringing up the situation with Xi. [...] Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China in recent years, winning U.S. President Donald Trump's approval for selling its H200 chips this year. It's unclear if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy those chips in large quantities. Nvidia said in a regulatory filing in August that it has sold only a small amount to China as such sales are restricted by the Chinese government.

items.title: Jensen Huang mất gần 7 tỷ USD vì bê bối ngoại tình - Báo VnExpress Kinh doanh
items.summary:
Dù vậy, Huang hiện vẫn nằm trong top 10 người giàu nhất hành tinh, với tài sản 155,4 tỷ USD. Ông sở hữu hơn 3,5% cổ phần Nvidia - công ty ông đồng sáng lập năm 1993 và đã làm CEO kể từ đó. [...] Chốt phiên giao dịch 9/11, cổ phiếu hãng chip Mỹ Nvidia giảm 4,27%. Trong phiên, mã này có thời điểm mất tới gần 7%. Diễn biến này khiến vốn hóa của Nvidia bốc hơi gần 200 tỷ USD, xuống còn 4.310 tỷ USD.

Tài sản của CEO Jensen Huang vì thế cũng giảm 6,8 tỷ USD chỉ trong một phiên. Ông cũng là tỷ phú mất tiền nhiều nhất thế giới hôm 9/11, theo thống kê của Forbes. [...] nghiệp, đối tác, cổ đông.
